release.source_note: Rust, card data and artwork match the frozen source used for the complete suites, release build, UI and API campaigns. Only historical Python source-check projection and an accidentally changed expected checksum were corrected before the second full Python run.

rules_review: The complete official SFD-139/221 face is Chaos Gear / Equipment, 3 Energy, no Power, +2 Might, Hidden and Equip one Chaos Power. Raw printing text is retained separately from its applicable Spiritforged erratum.

Core 811.1.d.1.a and 323.6 put Hidden gear at its battlefield and recall unattached non-Deploy gear during cleanup. Spiritforged FAQ/errata make here reminder text; Core 811.1.d.3/a retains original-field targeting while the gear is in base.
Normal play does not attach. Hidden reveal creates a mandatory friendly-unit target decision after entry, then an ordinary response window. Attachment and its Might bonus occur only on resolution.

A source that leaves play or a target that leaves the original Hidden field cannot be attached. A mandatory trigger with no legal target is not finalized. The unfinalizable case directly exercises the trigger filter after its target is removed.

Core 716–719 equipment follows the bearer and detaches when it leaves. Attached gear on any friendly unit at Orianna’s location satisfies her gear condition. Irelia choose/ready triggers remain separate.

An opponent’s Not So Fast cannot counter this attachment when it chooses only the controller’s own unit. The focused regression rejects the illegal counter; it does not claim successful counter coverage.
Bot views keep facedown identities private before reveal, then expose the public attachment decision, gear relationship and delayed Might consistently to both viewers. Validation cannot mutate state.

The sixth preset keeps legend identity 0 and the chosen champion within its 40 main cards. Sideboard cards stay out of its draw deck; all ten previous legend training recipes and the five previous preset recipes remain unchanged.
findings_resolved: Exact source-to-runtime mapping found the previously overlooked two Edge of Night copies.
The gear input path accepted a prematurely supplied attachment target; it now rejects that input atomically.

Initial focused fixtures required correction for power-pool integer type, combat priority, legal Not So Fast targeting and the timing of unfinalizable-trigger filtering. Final focused and complete suites pass.
Initial native test compilation referenced a nonexistent inspector-scroll field and private Game selection state. The final smoke test uses existing inspector state and public App selections.

The first Python run had eight old source-prefix checks affected only by the additive preset schema. A narrow exact projection removes those two schema additions and preserves all prior card bytes under their original proof hashes. The ninth failure was an accidental expected-checksum digit change during count updates; the original checksum was restored. No historical proof hash was rewritten.
limitations: The sideboard is inspectable reference metadata and can inform a custom practice copy. Registered best-of-three matches and between-game sideboarding are not implemented.

The full card inventory is the accepted dated catalog. Current Rules Hub and Spiritforged errata parsed facts match it; unresolved duplicate live publisher printing IDs still prevent claiming a fresh full-gallery acceptance.
Supported coverage is 466 of 1079 accepted legal identities, with 613 unavailable. This update does not establish complete Standard rules parity or tournament-strength AI.
Individual combat attribution and broader advanced-opponent work remain unfinished.
